question: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out under which Viceroy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Curzon**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Partition of Bengal** was carried out in **1905** by **Lord Curzon**, who served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905**. This decision is considered one of the most controversial acts of his tenure. ***Hence, the statement regarding Lord Curzon is correct.***

• The partition was officially announced on **July 19, 1905**, and it was formally implemented on **October 16, 1905**. The British government claimed that the **Bengal Presidency**, which included **Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha**, was too large (with a population of nearly **80 million**) to be administered efficiently.

• The real political motive behind the partition was to weaken the **Indian National Movement**, which was centered in **Bengal**. By dividing the province, the British aimed to create a communal rift between the **Hindu-majority West Bengal** and the **Muslim-majority East Bengal and Assam**.

• **Lord Ripon (1880-1884)** was known for the **Ilbert Bill** and the **repeal of the Vernacular Press Act**. He is often called the **Father of Local Self-Government** in India. He was not associated with the 1905 partition. ***Hence, the option Lord Ripon is incorrect.***

• **Lord Lytton (1876-1880)** is remembered for the **Vernacular Press Act (1878)**, the **Arms Act (1878)**, and the **Second Anglo-Afghan War**. His term ended long before the partition occurred. ***Hence, the option Lord Lytton is incorrect.***

• **Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856)** is famous for the **Doctrine of Lapse**, the introduction of the **Railways (1853)**, and the **Post and Telegraph** system. He left India nearly half a century before the partition. ***Hence, the option Lord Dalhousie is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Swadeshi Movement:** The partition triggered the **Swadeshi Movement**, which focused on the **boycott of British goods** and the promotion of **Indian-made products**. Leaders like **Surendranath Banerjee**, **Bipin Chandra Pal**, and **Lala Lajpat Rai** played a pivotal role in this mass agitation.

• **Annulment of Partition:** Due to relentless protests and the rise of revolutionary activities, the **Partition of Bengal** was finally **annulled in 1911** by **Lord Hardinge II** during the **Delhi Durbar**.

• **Capital Shift:** In the same year (**1911**), the British government decided to shift the **capital of India** from **Calcutta** to **Delhi** to ensure better administrative control and to appease the sentiments of the people.

• **Cultural Impact:** **Rabindranath Tagore** composed the song **'Amar Sonar Bangla'** (now the national anthem of Bangladesh) as a mark of protest. He also encouraged people to tie **Rakhi** on each other's wrists as a symbol of **Hindu-Muslim unity** on the day the partition came into effect.

• **Formation of Muslim League:** One of the long-term consequences of the communal divide fostered by the partition was the formation of the **All India Muslim League** in **1906** at **Dacca** (now Dhaka) under the leadership of **Nawab Salimullah**.

**Important Points__**

• **Administrative Reforms of Curzon:** Apart from the partition, **Lord Curzon** is known for the **Ancient Monuments Preservation Act (1904)**, the establishment of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, and the **Indian Universities Act (1904)**.

• **Surat Split (1907):** The difference in opinion regarding the methods of the **Anti-Partition Movement** (Moderates vs. Extremists) eventually led to the **Surat Split** of the **Indian National Congress** in **1907**.

• **Geographical Division:** The **Eastern Province** included **Assam** and the districts of **Dacca, Rajshahi, and Chittagong**, with its capital at **Dacca**. The **Western Province** included **Bihar and Orissa**, with its capital at **Calcutta**.
